title: Drelincourt: religious in the strict sense is God alone; in a wider sense, honor paid for God's sake
source_text: XVII. Carolus vero Drelincurtius observat aliquid religiosum duplici modo dici: primo rigide & exacte, prout religio proprie significat id quod animas Deo religat, & modum illum colendi praescribit. Et hoc sensu solum Deum religiose colendum esse docet: nec ea ratione religiosum esse honorem quo Sancti coluntur, cum sit ejusdem plane speciei cum eo quo fideles in terra degentes colimus, & gradu solum ab eo differat. Sed quandoque Religiosum latiori significatu id omne dici quod non solum religionis essentiam constituit, sed etiam ex ea pendet, & ab ea fluit. Et sic Religiosum dici posse honorem, qui personis & rebus quibuscunque defertur Dei honorandi causa, quia, scilicet, vel divino cultui inserviunt, vel in eis elucent divinae gratiae & gloriae dona. Et hoc sensu concedit religiosum esse honorem quo Beatos Spiritus, & Sanctam Virginem Christi matrem colimus. Responsione ad quaestionem Petri le Camus Episcopi jam dicti pag. 27.
pass_a_gloss: Charles Drelincourt observes that something is called religious in two ways: first rigidly and exactly, as religion properly signifies that which binds souls to God and prescribes that manner of cultivating. And in this sense he teaches that God alone is to be cultivated religiously: nor is the honor by which the Saints are cultivated religious on that account, since it is plainly of the same species as that by which we cultivate the faithful living on earth, and differs from it only in degree. But sometimes Religious, in a broader meaning, is said of everything that not only constitutes the essence of religion but also depends on it and flows from it. And thus the honor can be called religious which is paid to any persons and things for the sake of honoring God, because they either serve the divine cult or the gifts of divine grace and glory shine in them. And in this sense he grants that the honor by which we cultivate the blessed spirits and the holy Virgin, the mother of Christ, is religious. In the reply to the question of Peter le Camus, the bishop already mentioned, page 27.
pass_b_english: Drelincourt uses religious in a strict sense for what binds the soul to God and sets the manner of worshiping him.
In that sense only God is worshiped religiously, and Saint-honor is the same kind as honor of living believers, higher only in degree.
In a wider sense, religious covers whatever hangs on religion and is done to honor God.
In that wider sense he allows the honor of blessed spirits and of Christ's mother to be called religious.

choices.english: for the sake of honoring God
choices.why: The wider sense is honor paid on God's account, not a second latria.
rejected: for the saint as last end
as mere courtesy with no relation to God
